title: A closing checkpoint that fails transiently (control_unavailable) leaves the grant open, so the next queued prompt parks in a Resume-only hold instead of being retried automatically
outcome: When a turn's closing checkpoint fails with a transient, retryable control error (for example control_unavailable), the host settles or retries that checkpoint safely, so the grant is closed or provably accounted. The next queued prompt is then admitted, or parked in a retrying wait that clears by itself when control returns. It is never left in a Resume-only hold that needs Greg. Truly uncertain or possibly-begun authority keeps its explicit hold. A test reproduces the 2026-10-05 case: a failed closing checkpoint, then a queued head withheld locally, and recovery without manual Resume once control returns.
acceptance: A production-path witness with scripted transport and clock reproduces the 2026-10-05 case: a turn's natural closing turn_checkpoint fails with control_unavailable and the next queued prompt is withheld. Its RED is recorded on the then-current master without the admission-retry fix (w-5a1a58299818): a Resume-only hold with no scheduled retry. Its GREEN is recorded on top of that fix: the park schedules the shared admission retry. The holder note names both bases.

When control returns, the scheduled retry recovers without Resume: the rebind's status reconciliation closes the prior grant exactly once with its cached report (or clears it when status shows it closed) before any new evaluate, and the head is admitted and delivered exactly once. A test shows it.

No new watchdog or timer: the recovery is the shared admission retry of engram_retry_schedule.rs. Its time bound and exhaustion hold are delivered for every shared retry kind by w-ac230a24d0d8, not separately here.
Truly uncertain or possibly-begun authority keeps its explicit hold: an uncertain grant, or a refused or mismatched recovery checkpoint, is never retried automatically. Tests show each.
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
